title: Test environments and the "it works on my machine" problem

videos.script: A program is never tested on its own. {{env}} It runs on a machine, with a clock, a time zone, a version of Python and a browser at the other end. All of that is its environment. {{four}} Most teams keep four of them: development, test, staging and production. Each one is a step closer to what the customers use. {{report}} In this lesson a booking closes early on one machine and works on another. The developer says it works on his machine. And he is right. {{two-runs}} You reproduce both results on your own laptop. You pin the clock, change one setting, the time zone, and the result flips. {{edge}} Then you find the moment booking really closes. It is three hours early. {{record}} Last, you learn to put the environment in every report, in five short readings. {{close}} After that, nobody has to argue about whose machine is right.
